name: Whiteboard diagram
summary: An architecture or feature diagram built box by box as each part is named. Semantic layout, no coordinates. The same scene also plays live on the tldraw canvas.
length: 20–45 s, one scene (or a silent diagram)
steps: Pick a look before drawing anything (docs/looks.md): 3–4 looks made up for this subject (a 1–3 word name + a ≤12-word line each), 1–2 palettes besides theirs, a backdrop that fits (anim sheet <video> --scene <id> --backdrops); write style.md and theme.json
List the parts and their connections; group them into frames (labelled regions)
Write scene.json objects with relative placement (rightOf, below, in) and arrows between anchors (box.right, box.top:0.3)
Optional narration.txt with a {cue:part} on each part's name; anim voice
Timeline: draw-on each box on its cue, then its arrows; anim lint (arrow-crosses, box-overlap)
anim canvas <video> --watch to see it drawn on tldraw while you edit

scaffold.narration: Here's how it works. {cue:input}Input comes in here, {cue:core}the core does the work, {cue:output}and the result comes out here.

sections.brief: Draw each box on its cue (draw-on), then its arrow.
